Joint upper/lower Gaussian maxima converge to independent Gumbels; if p is fixed and q grows, the two q-side maxima agree to o_P(1) after b_q centering, leaving max_{p}|N_i|. If p,q grow with a_q/a_p->gamma, continuous mapping gives max(G1+gamma G2,G3+gamma G4). Independent exponential representations produce squared integral CDF, with gamma=1 yielding the K1 law and gamma=0 shifted Gumbel. Chi-square concentration and Gaussian extreme moment bounds make norm ratio error o(L²(a_p)) even after growing-side scaling; variance transfers.
